one_liner: Lookup-table CPU kernels for 1-4-bit LLM weights; 2-6x faster token generation than llama.cpp Q2_K/Q4_0 at low thread counts.
what_it_does: T-MAC is a kernel library for mixed-precision matrix multiply (int1/2/3/4 weights x int8/fp16/fp32 activations) aimed at low-bit LLM inference on CPUs. It is not a standalone drop-in: kernels are generated and tuned per model shape with TVM (Python), built into a C++ library, and consumed through a patched llama.cpp fork (-DLLAMA_TMAC=ON) after converting the model to a T-MAC GGUF. An all-in-one tools/run_pipeline.py drives compile, convert, build and run.
how_it_is_fast: Instead of dequantizing weights and doing multiply-add, it groups weight bits (e.g. 4 one-bit weights), precomputes all partial sums of the activations into a lookup table, and replaces MACs with table lookups (ARM tbl / x86 pshufb) plus shift-and-accumulate across bit planes. The table is halved (2^n to 2^(n-1)) using a sign bit. Cost scales linearly with weight bit-width, so 2-bit and 1.58-bit models gain far more than 4-bit ones.
when_to_use: Token generation (batch 1 GEMV) for 1-2-bit models such as BitNet b1.58 or W2 GPTQ/EfficientQAT models on ARM CPUs (Apple M-series, Snapdragon X, Jetson Orin, Raspberry Pi 5)
Edge deployments where you want the same tokens/s with fewer cores or less energy (README: 40 tok/s with 2 cores vs 8 for llama.cpp on Surface Laptop 7)
Low-thread-count inference: the gap is largest single-threaded (e.g. Raspberry Pi 5 BitNet-3B 8.03 vs 1.37 tok/s)
Prefill of W2 models on CPU without AMX (Surface Laptop 7 Llama-2-7B W2, 8 threads: 94.4 vs 21.3 tok/s llama.cpp, 37.7 with OpenBLAS)
when_not_to_use: 4-bit models at full thread count: the authors' own data shows only 1.09x (AGX Orin, 12 threads) and 1.13x (M2-Ultra, 8 threads) over llama.cpp Q4_0
Old-generation x86: the README warns it cannot guarantee meaningful speedup there, especially for 4-bit token generation
You need current upstream llama.cpp: integration is via a fork rebased to a 2024 llama.cpp; some models are unsupported by its convert script
Multi-batch GEMM on Apple M2-Ultra, where AMX-backed BLAS is comparable or faster
Simple builds: requires Python 3.8, building TVM from source (downloads clang+LLVM) and a per-model kernel compile step

integration.dependencies: TVM (built from source), Python 3.8 + virtualenv/conda, CMake >= 3.22, clang/LLVM (17.0.6 on Windows), patched llama.cpp submodule
integration.platforms: aarch64 (macOS, Linux, Windows on ARM, Android cross-compile), x86-64 (Linux, Windows); T-MAN variant targets Qualcomm NPU
integration.thread_safety: not documented (threading is through llama.cpp's -t threads)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — runs inside its llama.cpp fork with the same CLI (main/llama-bench), but models must be re-converted to a T-MAC GGUF with tuned kernel configs

gotchas: Kernels are tuned per model shape and quantization config (kcfg.ini); a new model means re-running the compile step (prebuilt ARM kernels via -u)
Published end-to-end numbers were measured on llama.cpp b2794 (May 2024) and without fast-aggregation; -fa adds 10-20% speed at some accuracy risk
llama.cpp throughput on Surface Laptop 7 was thermally unstable in 'Better Performance' mode, so some comparisons depend on the power profile
Open issues include a segfault (#98) and several build failures (missing t-mac-envs.sh, Windows CMake errors)
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick T-MAC over llamafile tinyBLAS when weights are 1-3 bit (tinyBLAS targets F16/Q8_0 prompt eval); pick MNN for general mobile model inference rather than low-bit LLM GEMV.
verified_claims_summary: Authors measured end-to-end token generation with T-MAC 2-bit vs llama.cpp Q2_K and T-MAC 4-bit vs llama.cpp Q4_0 (llama.cpp b2794) on Surface Laptop 7, M2-Ultra, AGX Orin, Raspberry Pi 5 and Surface Book 3; BitNet-3B on Surface Laptop 7 reached 20 tok/s on 1 core and 48 on 4 (README '4~5x'), while the EuroSys'25 paper states 'up to 4x' throughput and 70% less energy. Per-run compiler flags are not given.
status_note: MIT-licensed Microsoft Research project, stale since mid-2025 (last commit 2025-06-03) with 46 open issues; its ideas live on in microsoft/BitNet (bitnet.cpp), which the README says is powered by T-MAC.
